Advocates for pull incentives, such as subscription payments, that fund the development of and access to new antimicrobials against drug-resistant infections. Ambitious Impact published one public model of its work; the most recent, from June 2023, puts it at **<span data-figure="headline" data-model="alliance-for-reducing-microbial-resistance-aim">8.1</span> years of healthy life per $1,000**.

| Model | By | Date | Years of healthy life per $1,000 | Cells reproduced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ARMoR: advocacy for subscription models for new antimicrobials (Ambitious Impact, 2023 idea report)](/alliance-for-reducing-microbial-resistance) | AIM | June 2023 | <span data-figure="headline" data-model="alliance-for-reducing-microbial-resistance-aim">8.1</span> | 165 |

**Purely theoretical.** Ambitious Impact's estimate is of the idea, written before ARMoR (Alliance for Reducing Microbial Resistance) existed, not of the charity's own results. It is shown because ARMoR (Alliance for Reducing Microbial Resistance) runs the programme today ([checked October 2026](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/srjXGXhsecmZvpEdq/two-years-of-doing-advocacy-on-antimicrobial-resistance)) and no model of its actual work exists yet.

We haven't written our own evaluation of this charity yet. [How imported models work](/method#imported-models).
